_readme: THE SINGLE VERSIONED SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR WHAT REPAIR ASAP CHARGES.
This file is AUTHORED, not generated. It is immutable once released: a price change, a typo fix
and a withdrawn service are all a NEW version file, never an edit of this one. Old versions stay
in this repo forever so a lead quoted last month can still be verified against the prices it saw.
Everything downstream DERIVES from here: PriceItem rows, KnowledgeBase.services, the deterministic
price engine's floor, the text and voice AI prompt blocks, and (next phase) the website calculator.
Nothing downstream is allowed to restate a number.
SCOPE: this catalog belongs to ONE tenant, named in `tenantSlug`. lib/pricing/catalog.ts refuses to
hand it to any other organization. No other tenant can inherit these prices.
GAS IS FROZEN. Local Law 429 (2025) has required a Licensed Master Plumber for gas appliance
install/replacement since about 2026-02-22. Gas services carry status 'frozen', their cells are
copied byte-for-byte from calc-2026-08-01, they are exempt from the repricing AND from the $150
floor rule, and they produce no PriceItem and no KB entry. They are not removed.

startHereOnTheNextRepricing: READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING A SINGLE NUMBER. Everything below is measured from our own QuickBooks invoices, not from a market survey, and it is the strongest evidence this catalog has. A future repricing must start from it rather than rediscover it.

1. Our realised hourly rate is $82.05 weighted across 226.13 measured hours and 49 line items. We have NEVER billed an hour above $95. The NYC market band of $125-$165 is a repositioning of +52% to +101%, not an alignment.
2. The trend is DOWN: $86.72 in 2025, $76.46 in 2026. Do not assume drift toward the market.

3. Crew work is the exception and the only place we reach the bottom of the market band: $102.43 per man-hour over 144 man-hours of two-person renovation days, best line $129.69. This is what justifies the second-technician escalator and nothing else does.

4. 68 of 228 invoices carrying labor (30%) were completed BELOW the $150 work minimum, and 28 of those were below even the $99 assessment fee. Applying the floor is a real price rise on a third of our jobs, worth roughly $2,434/yr at current volume — it is not a formality.
5. Our realised assessment-visit price is $90, not $99 (11 invoices at exactly $90 labor). $99 is a deliberate +10% step first used on 2026-07-06 and is well supported.

6. THERE IS NO COST SIDE. ContractorPayout has 0 rows, there are 6 expense receipts totalling $306.96 and none of them is job-linked, and there is no wage field. Nobody can compute margin from this database. Do not let any number in this catalog be described as a margin, a markup or a profitability judgement — every floor here is measured against the owner's rules.

7. Where our own realised median exceeds what we publish, our books win. That happened twice in this release (furniture assembly, floating shelf) and both were raised on 2026-08-02. The drift test enforces it: see CATALOG_BELOW_REALISED in tests/unit/pricing-catalog-contract.test.ts.

8. Beware keyword matching against invoice descriptions. Most line items are named "General Handyman Services" or "Service Call" and the real scope is in the description, where renovation bundles casually mention other trades. One such mis-match put a $854 median on electrical troubleshooting in the previous pass; the true median is $80.
